about: Which contexts an Apple accelerator build serves (make_accelerator_serves.py, reference manifest30.serves; SPEC.md 5.4, README section 17; from SDK 3.0.2). Each case: `manifest` is the exact text of a manifest.json (UTF-8), `sha256` its SHA-256, `expect` what every SDK of the 3.0 line does with it when it trusts only `public_key_hex` (all are accepted: the rule adds nothing to the signed text). `serves`: for the builds `coreml` and `coreml-compact` and every context of the manifest, `served` (the build is fetched and tried for that context), `by` ("tolerance": a signed entry under <build>:<context>; "keep table": a file of role coreml-keeps for that context; null when not served) and `tolerance_key` (the key of the signed entry the golden stage uses, or null: tokens only). The listed files do not exist; every manifest is named as a build of model v4.0 with its four contexts.

cases.name: a package without keep tables
cases.about: Both Apple packages are listed for every context and no keep table is listed. The fp16 build serves the three contexts it has a signed tolerance for, the compact build two; c8_l64 runs on the CPU engine and nothing of a package is fetched for it.

cases.name: keep tables and the plain key
cases.about: A build as model 4.0.0 has them: a keep table for three contexts and one tolerance per build. It is served as before 3.0.2, by its keep tables, and judged by the plain key.

cases.name: keep tables and no tolerance
cases.about: The same without a tolerance: served by the keep tables and judged on tokens only, as before.

cases.name: a keep table for one context, a key for another
cases.about: c16_l64 is served by its keep table and judged by the plain key; c24_l256 is served by its own key and judged by it; c24_l72 and c8_l64 have neither.

cases.name: a key and a keep table for the same context
cases.about: The key decides: the context is served by it and judged by its tolerance, not by the plain key's.

cases.name: the tolerance is not signed
cases.about: The field is in the JSON and the signature covers the text without its lines: the tolerance counts as absent, its keys with it, so the packages serve no context.

cases.name: a malformed entry
cases.about: The entry for c16_l64 is not well formed (a string for a number): it has no signed line and names nothing. The entry for c24_l256 stands.

cases.name: a key for a context the manifest does not have
cases.about: c32_l64 is not one of `contexts`: its key names nothing.

cases.name: keys for a build whose package is not listed
cases.about: The compact build has keys and no package file: it serves no context.

cases.name: a context an SDK's own list called CPU only
cases.about: c8_l64 has a key: the build is tried for it. No list of contexts written into an SDK overrides what the manifest signs.

cases.name: a keep table for a context an SDK's own list called CPU only
cases.about: The same for a build with keep tables: a keep table listed for c8_l64 means the build is tried for it.

cases.name: identical tokens, written as a tolerance
cases.about: No build is served without a signed entry. A context that is to be judged on identical tokens has an entry of zero edits with the widest distances (30.0); a head the entry leaves out is judged on zero edits anyway.

cases.name: a package listed for one context
cases.about: The package's files are listed for c16_l64 only (not "*"): a key for another context finds no package and names nothing.

cases.name: no key and no keep table
cases.about: A package and nothing that names a context: no context is served, on every SDK. (Before 3.0.2 the same: no keep table, no promotion.)
